# Hereditary spastic paraplegia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Neurology > Movement disorders > Hereditary spastic paraplegia*

[Original Article Link](/library/oR00Lf)

---

## Summary

Hereditary <u>spastic</u> <u>paraplegias</u> (<u>HSP</u>) are a rare group of inherited <u>neurodegenerative diseases</u> which mainly affect the longest <u>axons</u> of the <u>corticospinal tract</u> and the <u>dorsal column</u> (which supply the lower limbs). <u>HSP</u> is caused by defects in <u>genes</u> which code for <u>proteins</u> essential for fast axonal neurotransmission. <u>HSP</u> can affect any age group. Patients present with <u>upper motor neuron</u> palsy of bilateral lower limbs, gait abnormalities, and <u>urinary urgency</u>/<u>urge incontinence</u>. <u>Dorsal column</u> dysfunction is usually mild. Additional neurological features such as <u>epilepsy</u>, <u>peripheral neuropathy</u>, or <u>cerebellar signs</u> may be present (complicated <u>HSP</u>). Diagnosis is mainly clinical. <u>MRI</u> of the spinal cord may demonstrate spinal cord <u>atrophy</u>. Treatment is mainly supportive, with <u>skeletal muscle relaxants</u>, <u>botulinum toxin</u>, and <u>physiotherapy</u> for muscle <u>spasticity</u>. <u>HSP</u> may be nonprogressive (childhood-onset) or progressive (adult-onset). Patients with progressive <u>HSP</u> are often wheelchair-bound by the age of 70 years. Patients with <u>HSP</u> have a normal life-expectancy.

---

## Clinical features

### Pure <u>HSP</u> (Uncomplicated <u>HSP</u>)




Pure <u>HSP</u> is characterized by an insidious onset and slow progression of the following symptoms




* <u>Upper motor neuron</u> <u>paralysis</u> of bilateral lower limbs

* <u>Spasticity</u>/hypertonicity → <u>contractures</u>

* Decreased muscle strength

* Gait abnormalities: delayed initiation of walking (childhood onset <u>HSP</u>); scissor gait (late onset <u>HSP</u>)

* Brisk <u>deep tendon reflexes</u>; <u>extensor plantar reflex</u> (<u>Babinski sign</u>)

* <u>Dorsal column</u> dysfunction in bilateral lower limbs (usually mild; only detected on examination): decreased/<u>loss of vibration sense</u>, 2-point discrimination sense, and position sense

* <u>Urinary urgency</u> and <u>urge incontinence</u>





### Complicated <u>HSP</u>




Patients with complicated <u>HSP</u> have all the features of pure <u>HSP</u> as well as additional neurological features, such as:




* <u>Epilepsy</u>, <u>intellectual disability</u>, <u>dementia</u>

* <u>Cerebellar</u> or <u>extrapyramidal symptoms</u>

* <u>Peripheral neuropathy</u>

* Loss of <u>vision</u>
